query: What kinds of expenses tend to get declined, and does it differ by department?

per_column.name: expense_category_type
per_column.rationale: Cleanly separated, interpretable expense-type categories (hardware, travel, software) that can be segmented and compared against decline rates and crossed with department.

per_column.name: asset_subcategory
per_column.rationale: Finer but still human-readable asset categories with well-populated buckets, enabling meaningful comparison of decline propensity across item types.

per_column.name: asset_brand
per_column.rationale: Interpretable vendor/brand segmentation with reasonable spread; decline patterns by brand are an informative exploratory angle.

per_column.name: entry_generation_method
per_column.rationale: Manual vs auto-generated is a clear, well-balanced binary that plausibly relates to declines (data-quality/process angle) and can be grouped on.

per_column.name: has_source_id
per_column.rationale: Presence/absence of source id is a well-separated binary provenance flag that can be compared against decline rates.

per_column.name: ci_identifier_quality
per_column.rationale: Interpretable data-quality tiers (standard name vs placeholder vs opaque id) with balanced buckets; a natural correlate of declines.

per_column.name: is_premium_or_high_end
per_column.rationale: Interpretable cost-tier flag; imbalanced (445/55) but still large enough to compare decline rates for premium vs standard items.

per_column.name: is_new_procurement
per_column.rationale: Interpretable procurement-context flag; identical 445/55 split to is_premium suggests possible redundancy, but conceptually a distinct segmentation.

per_column.name: travel_context_flag
per_column.rationale: Clear travel-vs-non-travel binary that segments expenses and can be compared against declines; partially overlaps expense_category_type but adds a usable axis.

judge.rationale: The set provides a strong, coherent collection of external, interpretable segmentation variables around declines: expense type, asset subcategory, brand, provenance/data-quality flags, cost tier, and travel context. Categories are well-separated and human-readable, and none merely restate state_declined. Combined with the existing department column, they directly support exploring what gets declined and how it differs by department. Minor deductions: is_premium_or_high_end and is_new_procurement share an identical 445/55 split hinting at redundancy, and travel_context_flag overlaps with expense_category_type, so the effective number of independent informative axes is somewhat less than nine.
